content: Finally, Figure shows the impact of decreasing the amount of training data in the detection scenario. It shows the difference in precision, recall, and F1-score with respect to that obtained using 100% of the training data. A general downward trend can be observed, as one would expect: less training data leads to less accurate predictions. However, the BERT-based model is the most robust to training-data reduction, showing an steadily low performance loss. With 1% of the dataset (230 training instances), the BERT-based model only suffers a striking 7-point F1-score loss, in contrast to the 32 and 39 points lost by the CRF and spaCy models, respectively. This steep performance drop stems to a larger extent from recall decline, which is not that marked in the case of BERT. Overall, these results indicate that the transfer-learning achieved through the BERT multilingual pre-trained model not only helps obtain better results, but also lowers the need of manually labelled data for this application domain.
